questions.question: Which of the following tribe belongs to Indo-European Linguistic family?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhili**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhili:-**

 
 
• **The Bhil are one of the largest tribal groups in India, primarily residing in the states of Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.**
 
• **They belong to the Indo-European Linguistic family.**
 
• They are also found in smaller numbers in Tripura, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Bhil tribes are mainly concentrated in the districts of Dhar, Jhabua, and West Nimar of Madhya Pradesh, and in Banswara and Chittorgarh districts of Rajasthan. A significant population also resides in the easternmost districts of Gujarat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Korwa:-**

 
 
• **The Korwa is an indigenous tribe largely found in the Indian states of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha. **
 
• Although they are spread across numerous states, their population is relatively small compared to other tribes.
 
 
 
• **Gondi:-**
 
 
• **The Gondi people are one of the largest Adivasi, or tribal groups, in India. **
 
• They are primarily found in the central region of India, within the states of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Garo:-**
 
 
• **The Garo are one of the major tribal communities in North-East India, predominantly inhabiting the Indian states of Meghalaya, Assam, and Tripura. **
 
• There are also Garo communities living in parts of Bangladesh adjacent to the Indian border.

questions.question: Which cultural festival of India held at Shilpgram, is a ten day feast of classical dances, folk art and light music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taj Mahotsav**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Taj Mahotsav Agra**, one of the most eagerly awaited festivals, is celebrated from **18th to 27th February** every year at** Shilpgram** near the Eastern gate of** “Taj Mahal”**.
 
• **Taj Mahotsav i**s an ode to the **rich cultural heritage **of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• In the **Taj Mahotsav **about **400 legendary artisans **from** different parts of the country **get an opportunity to display their **exquisite works** **of art**.
 
• The festival starts with a** road procession** with **decorated elephants** and **camels** like the **victory processions** of **Mughal emperors** and **warlords**.
 
• **Drum beaters, trumpet players, folk dancers, **skilled** craftsmen and artisans** also join the **procession**.** Artists** from all over India come here to display their art and **craftmanship**.
 
• Apart from the **exquisite craft work** you can experience the **majestic and magnetic performances** by artistes from every walks of life. The **soul-stirring performances** will **engulf** you to the **extent** of **casting a spell**.
 
• Throughout the Mahotsav, one can experience a** profusion of folk & classical music & dances of various regions,** especially the Brij Bhumi, performed the way they used to be centuries ago.
 
• The experience is so enthralling that one would not stop onesself from joining the dance with the **folk dancers**.
 
• Besides **folk music and dance**, the Mahotsav also exhibits the performance from the world renowned artists from** classical, semi-classical** and** popular art-forms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Natyanjali Utsav - **

 
 
• The spectacular annual dance festival** “Natyanjali” **is celebrated during **Mahashivaratri **in the months of **February** and** March** at **Chidambaram**.
 
• **Chidambaram** is also known as the "**city of the cosmic dancer" **as it is home to the **“Arulmigu Thillai Natarajar Temple”**, built in the **10th century by the Chola Dynasty**.
 
• The temple has a unique pillared hall with** Lord Natarajar sculptures** depicting **108 poses of Bharathanattiyam**. 
 
• Every year in the months of **February and March**, the **Natyanjali festival **honouring** Lord Shiva **is held on the grounds of the temple for** five days**. The whole of India's dance forms, including **Bharathanattiyam, Kuchupudi, Mohiniattam, Kathak, Odissi, Kathakali **and **Chhau**, are available to spectators under one roof.
 
• **The Natyanjali festival** is held every year with the intention of paying** homage to Lord Nataraja, the cosmic dancer**. The nation's populous dancers gather to perform in this festival as a tribute to **Lord Nataraja**. For many dancers, being able to perform their **"Arangettram"(first stage performance) **is a blessing.
 
 

 
• Nishagandhi festival - 

 
 
• The Nishagandhi festival is observed twice a year, once in the months of October and November and again in March and April.
 
• It takes place in the Nishagandhi Theatre within the grounds of Kanakunnu Palace in Trivandrum, Kerala.
 
• This festival lasts for roughly a week and attracts artisans from all around the nation.
 
• The Nishagandhi Dance Festival's artists who are committed to highlighting the rich diversity of Indian traditions are an essential component.
 
• The Kerala Tourist Development Corporation organizes the Nishagandhi Dance Festival.
 
• Other states occasionally co-host it as well.
 
• Recently, this celebration was co-hosted by West Bengal and Rajasthan.
 
• Other famous festivals of Kerala are - Onam,

 Attukal Pongala, Vishu, Thrissur Pooram, Theyyam Festival, Boat Race Festival, Makaravilakku, Adoor Gajamela.
 
 
 
• **Mamllapuram Utsav -** 
 
• The festival will be held at the **Shore Temple** in** Mamallapuram from December 23rd, 2022**, to **January 12th, 2023**. Get ready to experience the classical and** folk-art cultures **of** Tamil Nadu**.

questions.question: Which of the following national leaders of India inaugurated the first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh held in Ujjain in 1958?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, inaugurated the **first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh** in Ujjain in 1958.
 
• The event was organized to honor the legacy of **Kālidāsa**, one of the greatest Sanskrit poets and playwrights in Indian history.
 
• It was held in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, a city historically linked to Kālidāsa and considered a significant cultural and literary hub.
 
• The initiative aimed to celebrate Indian classical literature, art, and culture, and promote Sanskrit poetry and drama in modern times.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad, a renowned scholar himself, was deeply involved in promoting Indian heritage and culture during his presidency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kālidāsa:**

 
 
• Often referred to as the **Shakespeare of India**, Kālidāsa is celebrated for works like *Shakuntala*, *Meghadūta*, and *Raghuvaṃśa*.
 
• His literary works are deeply rooted in Indian culture, mythology, and philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Ujjain:**
 
 
• Ujjain, an ancient city in Madhya Pradesh, is historically associated with Sanskrit literature and figures like Kālidāsa.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage and as a center for learning and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samaroh:**
 
 
• The event is an annual celebration of classical literature, art, and culture in honor of Kālidāsa.
 
• It includes performances, scholarly discussions, and exhibitions showcasing Indian heritage.
 
 
 
• **Role of Rajendra Prasad:**
 
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was deeply committed to preserving and promoting India’s cultural and literary traditions.
 
• As the first President of India, he played a pivotal role in fostering national identity through art and culture.

questions.question: The ‘Ka Shad Mastieh’ or victory dance of the____________ tribe of Meghalaya is an ancient war dance performed during the prominent festival of the tribe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Khasi**.

__
 
• The 'Ka Shad Mastieh' or victory dance is a significant cultural dance of the **Khasi** tribe.
 
• This dance is an ancient war dance performed during the prominent festival of the Khasi tribe.
 
• It symbolizes victory and is an integral part of the Khasi's cultural heritage.
 
• The festival and the dance reflect the rich traditions and historical significance of the Khasi tribe in Meghalaya.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1
 The Bhoi tribe is another tribe in Meghalaya but they do not perform the 'Ka Shad Mastieh' dance.
 
 

 Option 2
 The War tribe is known for different cultural practices and does not perform the 'Ka Shad Mastieh' dance.
 
 

 Option 3
 The Khasi tribe performs the 'Ka Shad Mastieh' dance as part of their cultural festivities.
 
 

 Option 4
 The Jaintia tribe has its own distinct cultural dances and does not perform the 'Ka Shad Mastieh'.

questions.question: In the context of Sufi traditions, what is the meaning of the word 'sama'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Recitation of holy songs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the context of Sufi traditions, the meaning of the word 'sama' is the Recitation of holy songs**__.
 
• **Sama** is a Sufi ceremony performed as dhikr. Sama means "listening", while dhikr means "remembrance".
 __
 
• These performances often include singing, playing instruments, dancing, recitation of poetry and prayers, wearing symbolic attire, and other rituals.
 
• Sama is a particularly popular form of **worship in Sufism**.
 
• In 2008, UNESCO confirmed the "Mevlevi Sama Ceremony" of Turkey as one of the Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sufism**, also known as Tasawwuf, is a mystic body of religious practice within Islam characterized by a focus on Islamic spirituality, ritualism, asceticism, and esotericism.

questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mughal emperor who is often attributed with attempts to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora is:**
 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
 
• Aurangzeb, whose full name was **Abul Muzaffar Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb, ruled the Mughal Empire from 1658 to 1707.**
 
• He is known for his strict adherence to **Islam and the implementation of Islamic laws during his reign.**
 
• Aurangzeb was known for his military campaigns and extended the Mughal empire to its **greatest extent**.
 
• However, his** religious policies are often blamed for causing resentment among his Hindu subjects, which included the destruction or desecration of Hindu temples.**
 
• Reports suggest that he attempted to vandalise the** Kailash Temple at Ellora, an example of his iconoclastic policies, although the temple survived largely intact.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Kailasha Temple Ellora**

 
 
• ​__The Kailasha Temple is the largest of the rock-cut Hindu temples at the Ellora Caves, Maharashtra.
 
• It is considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world because of its size, architecture and sculptural treatment, and the climax of the rock-cut phase of Indian architecture.
 
• The Kailasa temple is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples and monasteries known collectively as the Ellora Caves, ranging for over 2 kilometers along the sloping basalt cliff at the site.
 
• The temple architecture shows traces of Pallava and Chalukya styles.
 
• The temple contains a number of relief and free-standing sculptures on a grand scale equal to the architecture, though only traces remain of the paintings which originally decorated it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
 

 Emperor
 Reign
 Important Works
 
 
 
 

 Humayun
 1530-1540, 1555-1556
 Humayun is known for his contribution to Persian literature. He lost his kingdom in 1540 but regained it with the help of the Safavid dynasty of Persia in 1555.
 
 

 Shah Jahan
 1628-1658
 Shah Jahan is best known for commissioning the Taj Mahal, a mausoleum for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. He also constructed the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid, among other architectural feats.
 
 

 Babur
 1526-1530
 Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, is known for his memoir, the Baburnama, which provides detailed insights into his life and times. He also established the basis for Mughal architecture in India.
